title: Spaghetti alle Vongole
subtitle: Clams, white wine, garlic, and pasta
excerpt: Clams steamed open in white wine and garlic, tossed with spaghetti and their briny juices. One of the definitive pasta dishes of southern Italy, no cream, no cheese, no shortcuts.

recipe.sourceNotes: Spaghetti alle vongole is a Neapolitan and Roman classic, though its roots run deeper through coastal Italy. The dish exists in two versions: bianco (white, without tomato) and rosso (with tomato). The bianco version, presented here, is considered the purer expression. The clam juice is the sauce.

recipeTools.notes: With a lid, for steaming the clams.

content.text: Spaghetti alle vongole depends entirely on fresh clams. The clams steam open in white wine and release their liquid, which is the sauce. There is nothing else providing flavour, just garlic, a little chilli, parsley, and the pasta's starch. Soak the clams in cold salted water for an hour before cooking to purge any sand.

items.preparation: scrubbed, soaked in cold salted water for 1 hour

content.text: Drain and rinse the clams. Discard any that are open and do not close when tapped. Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water. Reserve a large cup of pasta water before draining, 2 minutes before it is cooked through.
While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large wide pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until softened but not coloured.
Turn the heat to high. Add the clams and wine. Cover immediately and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the pan, until all the clams have opened. Discard any that stay closed.

Add the drained spaghetti directly to the pan with the clams. Toss together over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, adding pasta water to create a glossy sauce that coats the pasta. Scatter over the parsley and serve immediately in warm bowls. No cheese.
